name: Methyldiazinol

lead: Methyldiazinol is an obscure oral steroid synthesised in the 1960s as a modified version of mestanolone. It was never sold as a drug.
The only reported pharmacology is an old animal measurement suggesting a high muscle-to-androgenic ratio.

paras: It is a 17α-methylated DHT analogue with a diazirine group at carbon 3; its mechanism has not been described beyond presumed androgen activity.
No human safety data exist and it has no approved use.

lead: Methyldiazinol (3,3-azo-17α-methyl-5α-dihydrotestosterone, or 3-azi-17α-methyl-DHT) is a synthetic, orally active androgen and anabolic steroid that was never marketed [1]. It is a 17α-methyl derivative of dihydrotestosterone, specifically the 3-azi (diazirine) analogue of mestanolone [1].

It is described in a 1965 paper by Church, Kende and Weiss on the preparation of steroid diaziridines and diazirines [1]. Wikipedia reports a muscle-building to androgenic ratio of 15 relative to oral methyltestosterone, among the highest recorded in the old animal literature [1].
Only that early animal-era data and chemistry exist; no human studies have been published.

paras: The only available pharmacology is a historical animal bioassay ratio of myotrophic to androgenic activity, reported as about 15 relative to methyltestosterone [1]. Mechanism and human pharmacokinetics have not been described [1].

timeline.event: Described by Church, Kende and Weiss in the Journal of the American Chemical Society [1].
